Your governments already waste $12.6K per person per year (Political Dysfunction Tax political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025). Sitting this out is a bet that everything in the Problem Statement fixes itself. Look at the Problem Statement and decide how confident you are.

For Context on "Political Donations"

On your planet, humans give papers to politicians and receive nothing back except a warm feeling and occasionally a hat. This deposit grows at 17.4% annually, reaching 11.1x by 2040, and you keep it if the targets are missed. On Wishonia, we would call your current system "giving money to strangers who do not give it back." You call it "democracy."

You do not need to tip the scale by yourself. The stakes are so large that even a tiny nudge is worth real money:

| Your unreimbursed contribution | Break-even probability shift (Treaty floor) | Break-even probability shift (Wishonia) |
|---|---|---|
| $1K | 0.0067% | 0.0019% |
| $10K | 0.067% | 0.019% |
| $100K | 0.671% | 0.192% |
| $1M | 6.71% | 1.92% |

But does a $1K contribution actually shift probability by 0.0067%? You do not need to be the marginal dollar that tips the scale. You need to believe that more campaign capital makes success more likely than less, which is basically obvious. Those thresholds also treat PRIZE deposits like unreimbursed spending, so they are biased against contributing. They survive heavy skepticism: if you think the per-capita gain is 100x smaller than modeled, the break-even for $1K is still only 0.67%. The math does not require trusting the model. It requires believing the model is not off by more than four orders of magnitude. And the ceiling cost is already bounded: $1B for the 1% Treaty campaign, or $128B to optimize all public policy globally (see Problem Statement).

"Pay people if the outcome happens" and "act once enough others commit" are not new ideas tabarrok1998. The Chenoweth threshold (3.5%) is the historical floor for when movements become hard to ignore. The RECOVERY trial was run by Oxford and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Every building block is peer-reviewed. The combination is new.

The free-rider problem has a structural answer. "VOTE points only pay if the targets are met, so if I don't believe they'll be met, there's no incentive." This assumes VOTE points are the only incentive. They are not. PRIZE deposits beat conventional retirement on the failure branch (11.1x vs. 2.57x). The deposit incentive works regardless of your belief about success. VOTE points add upside on the success branch.

But the deeper answer is that free-riding makes sense when participation is expensive. Clicking a button takes 30 seconds. This referendum pays $8.44K and cures diseases. I suspect the participation problem solves itself.

I am told humans need time to "evaluate" arithmetic. The arithmetic is patient. The diseases are not.

The selfish reason to play the Game is not the VOTE payout or the pool return. It is that you personally get $6.74M richer in a world where diseases get cured.

How the Game Spreads

Everything below this point (the lobbying, the treaty campaigns, the clinical trial infrastructure, the decentralized FDA dfda-spec-paper-2025; Sinn) is not your job. 4 billion people whose payout depends on curing diseases will attract the lobbyists, researchers, and institutions who know how to cure diseases. You do not need to understand lobbying or clinical trial design. You need to understand that a large enough pile of money pointed at "cure diseases" attracts the people who do. This is how your species built every industry it has. Nobody coordinated the smartphone supply chain. The money coordinated it.

1. A host launches the Planetary Constitutional Convention planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025. The manual gets stress-tested. PRIZE deposits begin. You deposit and recruit. (This is the hard part. Everything after this is money doing what money does.)
2. The referendum opens. Voters set their preferred military-to-health allocation. Every recruiter who brings a verified participant earns VOTE points. The referendum grows because recruitment is rewarded. On your planet, this is called "going viral." On Wishonia, it is called "obvious."
3. The Scoreboard climbs. Votes, treaty support, pool size, and the two numbers. Each new name makes the next name easier. Your species calls this "momentum." We call it "counting."
4. The lobbying campaign starts itself. Millions of people whose payout depends on the treaty attract lobbyists and institutions because the pool makes showing up profitable. (Implementation financing earth-optimization-protocol-2025.) Nobody organizes this centrally. The money organizes it, the same way nobody centrally organizes which restaurants open in your city. The restaurants that serve food people want get money. The restaurants that don't, close. You are building the restaurant version of not dying.
5. Implementation. Governments move the money. People compete to cure diseases cheaply. Not your job. Your job was step 1. You can go back to arguing about Pluto now.

Each stage builds the audience for the next. Nobody coordinates this centrally. The incentives coordinate it. For the institutional deployment plan and activation budget, see Why Your Institution Should Be The Initiating Node.

How the Papers Move (Follow the Money, Try to Keep Up)

Everything the Game exists to produce is either healthy life years or more papers. Paying for moving budgets around or enrolling people in trials is paying for plumbing that may or may not deliver water. Your species has a long history of buying plumbing and then celebrating the plumbing while the house burns down. (You call this "overhead.") Pay for water.

Your PRIZE pool trigger. By 2040: targets met, the pool distributes to VOTE point-holders; targets missed, depositors divide it pro rata.

Why better ideas win. The Prize pays for outcomes, not methods. Every proposal in this manual (the treaty, the bonds, the Prize Fund, the decentralized FDA dfda-spec-paper-2025; Sinn) is improvable plumbing. If someone finds a cheaper way to move the two numbers, VOTE point-holders shift recruitment toward it because it makes them more money. The two numbers do not change. The plumbing is replaceable. That is the point.

Why Nobody Needs to Understand This Manual

One of your economists once held up a pencil on television and said: "There's not a single person in the world who could make this pencil. The wood comes from a tree in Washington. The graphite comes from mines in South America. The rubber comes from Malaya. The brass ferrule, I haven't the slightest idea where it came from. Literally thousands of people cooperated to make this pencil. People who don't speak the same language, who practice different religions, who might hate one another if they ever met. No one sitting in a central office gave orders to these thousands of people. No military police enforced the orders that were not given." [-Friedman and Friedman]

Your species already understands this for pencils. The Game applies it to not dying.

Look at this cured disease. There is not a single person in the world who could cure it. The researcher in Lagos who found the cheaper trial design does not know the lobbyist in Brussels who passed the directive. The lobbyist does not know the nonprofit in Manila that recruited a million voters. The voters do not know the bondholder in New York whose greed funded the campaign. The bondholder does not know the politician in Delhi who voted yes because the SuperPAC funded her opponent last time she voted no. The politician does not know the factory worker in Dhaka whose clinical trial enrollment generated the data that proved the treatment worked. Literally millions of people cooperated to cure this disease. People who do not speak the same language, who practice different religions, who might hate one another if they ever met. No one sitting in a central office gave orders. No military police enforced the orders that were not given. Two numbers on a Scoreboard and pieces of paper with presidents on them did what no committee, no charity, and no central plan has ever done.

How Many Papers Does It Take to Save a Species

What does it cost to get the Game to scale? Here is what it costs to pay 4 billion people to click a button:

The planning midpoint is $30B: a blended reward of $5 per verified participant, plus $1.5 to verify everyone is real and pay them, plus $4B in fixed platform and launch costs.

How large does your pool get? It starts at whatever gets deposited and compounds through the Prize Fund at 17.4% annually. Global investable financial assets total $305T (equities, bonds, cash, and investment funds). At 1% participation, the pool compounds to:

One percent of the investable pool. One percent of the military budget. The entire proposal asks for 1% of two things your species already has. One percent of your weapons money and one percent of your savings. That both numbers are "1%" is not a coincidence. It is the smallest amount that compounds into something worth arguing about.

How big does the pool need to be before two VOTE points are worth more than a retirement account?

$1.8T. That is when it becomes personally obvious, not the minimum to get started.

What does a VOTE point pay? The modeled coordination target is 50% of humanity:

At that headcount, 4 billion people participate and split the pool based on how many people they recruited. One referred voter is one point. The payout per VOTE point (at 1% participation):

Why this referendum beats your elections

| Dimension | Your elections | This referendum |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Effort | Hours in line, research candidates | 30 seconds on a phone |
| Financial reward | $0 | $8.44K modeled success payout |
| Your vote matters | ~1 in 30 million chance of mattering gelman2012 | Direct payout proportional to contribution |
| What happens after | Politician may ignore you (they will) | Money goes where the Scoreboard says |

Your species turns out at 50-65% for elections despite getting paid nothing. This referendum pays you if it works, credits you for who you recruited, and publishes the score.

Why more pools make everyone richer. Your protocol does not need a single pool. It needs a single metric standard. Any pool that measures the same two outcomes (healthy life years, median income) and checks that each person is real automatically joins the reward network. A verified person claims proportionally from every participating pool, regardless of which one recorded their vote. Japan launches a pool, the EU launches a pool, the Gates Foundation launches a pool. The combined reward grows with each new entrant. A "competing" pool is actually a deposit. Spending money to "attack" the network is indistinguishable from donating to it. Think of email: you can run your own server; all servers interoperate; running your own extends the network rather than fragmenting it.

What your protocol must solve. Six things: (1) verify each person is real and only counts once, (2) register pools, (3) split payouts across pools, (4) add up the Scoreboard, (5) measure the two numbers, (6) pay people. The protocol specification earth-optimization-protocol-2025 has the details.

Why Everyone's Greed Points the Same Direction

Your politicians care about reelection. Your investors care about returns. Your citizens care about not dying. This is not a design flaw. It is a design constraint. Here is how you work with it instead of against it:

- Depositors put money in because they get it back (at 11.1x) if this fails. If it succeeds, diseases get cured and they are $6.74M richer.
- Recruiters recruit because every person they bring in earns them a VOTE point.
- Entrepreneurs compete for a giant implementation contract.
- Politicians get funded for voting yes and watch their opponents get funded if they vote no (details below).
- Researchers compete to prove what works.
- Citizens get a 30-second vote that might pay $8.44K.

Every participant is doing exactly what they would do anyway, except pointed at diseases instead of each other.

The politician line is the one that requires explanation, because "politicians notice a Scoreboard" has never caused a politician to act against their donors. Here's what converts Scoreboard scale into treaty passage: the Incentive Alignment Bond iab-paper-2025. IABs raise the campaign capital ($1B). Investors buy bonds. The campaign passes the treaty. The treaty redirects $27.2B/year from military budgets to clinical trials. A management fee on that flow splits three ways: 10% back to investors as a revenue share (272% annual returns, which is not a typo), 10% to a SuperPAC that funds treaty-aligned politicians and post-office careers for yes-voters, and 80% to clinical trials through wishocratic allocation where nobody with money gets to decide where it goes. The investors become the world's most motivated lobbyists for expanding the treaty, because their returns grow with it. The politicians face the same incentive structure that the NRA perfected, pointed at "not dying" instead of "more guns." The loop is self-sustaining: investor greed funds the campaign, campaign greed passes the treaty, treaty revenue feeds investor returns, investor returns fund more campaigns. Nobody has to become good. The money just circulates until diseases stop existing. This is your species' greatest talent put to its first good use. (For the full mechanism, see Incentive Alignment Bonds iab-paper-2025.)

Frequently Asked Objections (Your Species Has Many)

I have presented this game to many humans. They have objections. I have collected the objections below, along with my confusion about each one.### 1. "The targets are insanely ambitious"

The Game's targets are the Treaty floor, not a world with optimal governance. HALE of 85 years (+21.7 healthy years) and median income of $76.7K (4.17x your current lifetime earnings) are what the model produces from a single intervention: redirecting 1% of military spending to clinical trials. A world that deploys Incentive Alignment Bonds across every policy domain, eliminates the political dysfunction tax entirely, and lets citizens allocate budgets directly through wishocratic allocation reaches 90.1 years HALE, $504K median income (44x current lifetime earnings), and GDP at 26.9x the status quo trajectory (see GDP Trajectories gdp-trajectories-paper-2025 and Wishonia for what that world looks like). The Prize triggers at the floor, not the ceiling.

The $76.7K is compound arithmetic from two mechanisms running simultaneously for 15 years: (1) military-to-R&D redirect ($27.2B/year) with a 2x spillover multiplier from your own published studies, and (2) disease-burden recovery (preventable disease currently drags 13% of GDP; each cure permanently unlocks a slice of that $15 trillion). Year one, the redirect produces twice its value in adjacent-sector growth. Year two, you have last year's redirect plus recovered productivity from diseases the trials identified treatments for. Year three, bigger again. By year five the loop runs on its own output. This is the same compound interest your retirement account uses. The only difference is the return rate (see GDP Trajectories gdp-trajectories-paper-2025 for the full year-by-year derivation).

Cut every input in half. Cut them in quarters. The model still produces a civilization instead of a collapse, because no plausible adjustment to any single variable eliminates the effect of two compounding mechanisms running simultaneously for 15 years.6 years-77.1 years) and eliminates the efficacy lag. Anything beyond that (political dysfunction elimination, full governance optimization) pushes toward the Wishonia ceiling and is gravy.

Historical precedent your own species already proved: your grandparents cut military spending by 87.6% in two years after WWII ($1.42T to $176B in today's dollars) us-post-wwii-military-spending-cut. Factories switched from bombers to Cadillacs. The economy exploded into the greatest boom in human history us-post-wwii-gdp-growth-8-pct. "But the military-industrial complex didn't exist in 1945." Correct. That is why we budgeted $1B instead of $25M, and why Incentive Alignment Bonds iab-paper-2025 create a bondholder class whose income scales with treaty expansion. The MIC has a lobby. The IAB creates a counter-lobby with 272% returns. The difference between 1945 and 2026 is not that reallocation is harder. It is that you need to buy your way past the people who profit from the status quo. The budget accounts for this. They managed 87.6% during demobilization and built the middle class. We are asking for 1%.

I notice that the humans who find these targets "insanely ambitious" do not find the current 604:1 ratio insane. The ratio is familiar, so it is invisible. The solution is unfamiliar, so it looks crazy. I do not understand which part is ambitious.

2. "Treaties never work"

Your species has already banned entire weapons industries multiple times, without any greed-powered Incentive Alignment Bonds:

- Biological Weapons Convention (1972/1975): 187 countries outlawed an entire category of WMD.
- Chemical Weapons Convention (1993): 193 countries banned chemical weapons production and stockpiles.
- Ottawa Treaty (1997): 164 countries banned landmines. One woman with a phone and a coalition of NGOs did it in 14 months, despite major military powers opposing it icbl-ottawa-treaty.
- Cluster Munitions Convention (2008): same story, two years cluster-munitions-convention-2008.

None of these needed Victory Incentive Alignment Bonds or 272% returns. They passed because enough people got sufficiently annoyed. The 1% Treaty is easier: it keeps 99% of every military budget intact, the relative power balance unchanged, and it bribes everyone with massive personal upside. The Treaty Feasibility appendix shows historical campaign costs of $25-50M; we budgeted $1B with a benefit-cost ratio exceeding 259k cost-of-change-paper-2025.

I would be curious to hear why the version with financial incentives is considered less likely than the versions without.

3. "Goodhart's Law"

On your planet, there is a tradition of raising Goodhart's Law at this point in the conversation. I have come to recognize it as a signal that the human is thinking carefully, which I appreciate. The concern is not that HALE and median income are bad metrics. The concern is that any metric with hundreds of trillions riding on it will be gamed. Fair. Here is why it is harder than it sounds.

Mortality is binary and hard to fake across millions of people. You either died or you did not. Hospitals, insurance claims, mortality registries, and satellite-derived economic indicators all have to agree. Median income requires improving the middle of the distribution, not just the top; you cannot game it by making billionaires richer.

The protocol earth-optimization-prize-protocol-paper-2025 specifies three structural defenses: (1) methodology lock-in at baseline, so any WHO or World Bank methodology change requires re-baselining and resets the improvement clock; (2) minimum population coverage (data must represent at least 80% of the global population, so you cannot improve the number by excluding the sick or poor); and (3) decentralized survey cross-checks using the voter base itself, adding a methodology-independent data stream collected directly from millions of humans. One person lying has approximately zero effect on the median. This is statistics, not voting.

The Optimitron optimocracy-paper-2025 adds five independent measurement sources (census, federal reserve, labor statistics, academic institutions, decentralized citizen surveys) where corrupting all simultaneously requires bribing five institutions that hate each other. The adversarial challenge window means anyone who catches gaming can post a bond, present evidence, and claw back the payout.

I have been watching your planet for 81 years and have not heard a better pair of numbers proposed. If you have one, the protocol is open source. The alternative is the current path: half the economy looted by 2040 while 55 million die yearly.

4. "The implementation is impossibly complex"

Humans tell me this is "impossibly complex." I have listed the six capabilities the protocol requires. All of them already exist at scale:

| Capability needed | What already does this |
|:---|:---|
| Identity layer (one person, one vote) | KYC bank accounts. Your species verifies identity billions of times daily for far less important reasons than curing disease. |
| Pool registry | Investment funds. Vanguard manages $9T across millions of accounts. A prize pool is a fund with a conditional payout trigger. |
| Cross-pool claim settlement | Interbank settlement. SWIFT processes $5T/day across 200+ countries. Splitting a pool pro rata is simpler than a wire transfer. |
| Scoreboard aggregation | Election results dashboards. Every democracy already aggregates and publishes vote counts in real time. |
| Measure the two numbers | WHO and World Bank. They already publish HALE and median income annually. That IS the measurement. |
| Claim mechanics | Dividend payments. Corporations pay billions of shareholders quarterly. Paying VOTE point-holders once is simpler. |

The Game does not require inventing anything. It is a survey where you prove you are a real person, and a savings account that pays out if enough people convince their governments to stop wasting money. Legally, it is an escrow account with a payout trigger, not a security. The referendum could be a ballot measure; elections already exist. Enforcement: the treaty IS the enforcement, exactly like every other treaty your species has signed.

Your species moves $5 trillion across borders every day, verifies 8 billion identities, and counts 4 billion votes in elections. A survey with a savings account attached does not seem like the hard part.

5. "The 17.4% return is too good to be true"

The 17.4% is not a promise. It is transparent arithmetic from four independently sourced components: (1) 17% venture capital gross return (Cambridge Associates 25-year pooled IRR), (2) -2.5% scale compression drag (explicitly modeled for 15x market expansion; i.e., the model already penalizes itself for the skeptic's concern about diminishing returns), (3) +2.08% crowd allocation alpha (91% crowd accuracy vs. 65% for expert fund managers surowiecki-2004; the S&P SPIVA scorecard confirms 88% of actively managed large-cap funds underperformed the S&P 500 over 15 years spiva2023), and (4) +0.8% from eliminating home-country bias (70+ countries each overweight domestic assets, missing global diversification; IMF/Vanguard estimate 0.3-1.5% annual drag). The structural advantage is not a feedback loop or a hope. It is arithmetic from removing fees, removing the accreditation wall, and letting crowds allocate. See Earth Optimization Prize Fund for the full derivation.

6. "272% returns is a scam"

To anyone in finance, "272% annual returns" sounds like a red flag. Good. It should sound unusual. It is not a market return. It is a political-risk premium. The math: the treaty redirects $27.2B/year. A 10% management fee = $2.72B/year. The campaign costs $1B. $2.72B / $1B = 272%. The appropriate comparison is not the S&P 500. It is the return on any binary political bet that hits: lobby for a policy, the policy passes, you capture a percentage of the resulting revenue flow. Lobbying returns routinely exceed 100:1 when they work lobbying-roi-calc. The 272% is contingent on the treaty actually passing, which is the hard part. The transparency is the defense: every number is disclosed, not hidden. And the bondholders become the world's most motivated lobbyists for expanding the treaty, because their returns grow with it. The mechanism that looks like a red flag is the mechanism that makes your treaty durable. (For the full derivation, see Incentive Alignment Bonds iab-paper-2025.)

7. "The VOTE payout is too large/too small"

The modeled VOTE point value is $8.44K at 1% of global investable assets ($305T). That confidence interval ($8.44K) reflects the real uncertainty: how much capital flows into the pool. At 0.1% participation, a VOTE point pays hundreds of dollars. At 10%, tens of thousands. The model uses 1% as the central estimate because it parallels the treaty ask (1% of military spending) and because asking people to redirect 1% of their invested savings into a higher-returning vehicle is not an unusual ask.

The pool does not need to be large for the Game to be worth playing. It needs to be large enough that telling two people about it is worth 30 seconds. That is not a high bar. Your species spends more time than that choosing a sandwich.

8. "The 604:1 ratio cherry-picks the denominator"

The 604:1 compares government military spending ($2.72T) to government clinical trial spending ($4.5B). Government-to-government. The treaty redirects government money, so this is the correct like-for-like comparison.

"But industry funds 90% of clinical trials." Yes. And industry only tests drugs that can be patented and sold for high prices. Off-patent cures, orphan diseases, repurposed generics, and every disease that does not affect enough rich people get zero industry funding. The 604:1 measures the gap that only government can close. Even if you include all clinical trial spending ($60B), the ratio is still 45.3:1. That is not a rebuttal. That is a confession. (See Global Government Medical Research Spending for the full accounting.)

Quick answers

| Objection | Answer |
|:---|:---|
| "This will never work" | The treaty campaign costs $1B, with a societal benefit-cost ratio exceeding 259k cost-of-change-paper-2025. Even the ceiling cost of fixing everything (matching all opposition spending across all policy domains globally) is $128B, which a coalition of 3-5 decabillionaires could fund while keeping the vast majority of their wealth cost-of-change-paper-2025. "Political impossibility" is a capital allocation problem, not a physics problem. |
| "Does this require trusting one institution?" | No. A credible host can initiate the network, but it should not be the root of trust. The rules, contracts, interfaces, and measurement layers should remain open, forkable, and replaceable so another host can continue the process if the first one fails. |
| "Does hosting mean endorsing the current manual?" | No. The host endorses the process, not the draft. See Planetary Constitutional Convention. |
| "I'd lose my $1" | On failure, depositors divide the realized pool pro rata. On success, the deposit funds the pool by design. The selfish case is that the rest of your life got much larger than the dollar you put in. |
| "Can I sell my claim?" | Not inside the protocol. PRIZE stays with the depositor's verified account until resolution. VOTE stays with the verified recruiter who earned it. Private contracts can exist outside the protocol, like assigning future royalties, but the protocol does not broker or enforce them. |
| "Why can't PRIZE be withdrawn early?" | Because a redeem-anytime exit right would let depositors drain the pool as success became more likely. The Game only works if the capital remains committed until the measurement date. |
| "What if I die or lose access?" | Claims belong to a verified account, not a fragile device. The system needs account recovery, beneficiary designation, and lawful successor control so a 15-year claim does not disappear because you lost your phone or your heirs need to prove who they are. |
| "Nobody else will participate" | That IS the problem the Game exists to solve. Your deposit is the proof that someone does. The Scoreboard makes everyone else's participation visible. |
| "I don't understand the mechanism" | You do not need to. Vote, recruit 2 people. |
| "Why can't VOTE points be traded?" | Tradability would buy liquidity but invert the signal: outsiders could buy coalition credit without doing coalition work. The public signal this design relies on is simpler: verified participant count, referendum growth, and a visible pool of committed capital. |

Your mechanism does not need participants to be wise. It needs them to be self-interested, impatient, and capable of reading a scoreboard. The whole thing is open source.

Four treaties banned entire weapons industries without paying anyone to sign them. This one pays people. I still do not understand why the version with financial incentives gets more objections than the versions without.

The math does not require every reader. It requires enough readers to fill a scoreboard.

Earth Optimization Protocol v1

Humans are the contestants in the Earth Optimization Prize. This paper documents the current open-source instruction manual for helping humanity raise healthy life years and median income by 2040. Fork it and improve it to help humanity win faster.



Introduction

The system has eleven functions but only five organizations that someone has to actually be. The rest is software, protocol rules, and compound interest. Here are the five, why each exists, and why none of them can be the same entity as any other.

The Five Roles

1. The Starter (Launch Host). Makes the first public version of the Earth Optimization Prize real. Publishes the challenge rules, convenes the first expert review panel, funds adversarial-review bounties, and launches a live public scoreboard. This is the role that turns a stack of papers into inspectable public infrastructure. It is time-bounded by design: the Starter hosts the first 90-day cycle and then hands off or continues, but at no point becomes the permanent root of trust. One institution may start the network. No institution should be able to stop it. Redundancy model: sequential, not parallel. During bootstrap, one institution must go first or nobody goes at all (this is the current state; diffused ownership is why the prize is still a PDF). After the first cycle, co-hosts and successor hosts can join. Clear ownership during each bounded period, but replaceable between periods. (Full specification: The Initiating Node Memo and the 90-Day Pilot.)

2. The Vault (Pool Custodian). Holds PRIZE deposits, executes the published investment policy, and disburses funds when the oracle triggers release. This is custody, fiduciary duty, and independent audits. The Vault does not decide whether the targets were met. It does not lobby for the treaty. It does not know who the voters are. It holds money, invests it according to published rules, and moves it when told to by the Referee. That is all. Redundancy model: many parallel pools. The protocol treats multiple pools as complements, not competitors. Japan launches a pool, the EU launches a pool, the Gates Foundation launches a pool. Each pool has ONE custodian (clear ownership, someone to audit, someone to sue), but the system has MANY pools. A voter claims proportionally from every participating pool. Launching a "competing" pool is indistinguishable from donating to the network. A bad custodian loses depositors to a better pool. Markets handle discipline. (The custodian role is described in Decentralized Institutes of Health and the Legal Architecture.)

3. The Referee (Measurement Authority). Locks the baseline measurement methodology before the game begins, reads WHO and World Bank data at specified intervals, publishes cryptographically signed determinations of whether the graduated release thresholds have been met, and runs the dispute resolution process when someone challenges the data. The Referee decides whether the targets were hit. The Vault holds the money. These two jobs exist in separate organizations for the same reason you do not let the scorekeeper also be the team owner. Redundancy model: one accountable consortium, verified by many. The inputs are already multi-node (five independent data sources that produce the same answer if nobody is lying). The binding determination has to converge on one signed statement, but the computation is deterministic from public data, so anyone can verify it independently. If the Referee's determination disagrees with what the raw data says, the bonded challenge mechanism lets anyone post evidence and trigger independent review. The Referee is a single accountable node that is continuously auditable by everyone. (The measurement system is described in Optimocracy.)

4. The Bouncer (Identity Provider). Verifies that each referendum participant is one real human, not a bot, deepfake, or the same person registering twice under a different hat. Maintains or contributes to the global nullifier set (the shared log that prevents double-registration across pools). Without one-person-one-vote enforcement, VOTE points are meaningless and Sybil attacks transfer wealth from legitimate voters to attackers. The Bouncer cannot be the same organization as the Vault, because the entity that knows who people are should not be the entity that holds their money. Redundancy model: start with one, add more with bridging. The protocol defines a provider-agnostic interface so additional providers can be added without re-architecting. Multiple Bouncers add geographic resilience (if World ID gets banned in a jurisdiction, BrightID or government e-ID picks up). The shared state (global nullifier set) is append-only and public, so no single provider's disappearance destroys the voter registry. Each provider owns its verification process clearly; the protocol handles cross-provider deduplication.

5. The Sword (Campaign Executor). Converts scoreboard support into political action. Raises campaign capital via Incentive Alignment Bonds, operates the SuperPAC that funds treaty-aligned politicians, and coordinates the legal path from "public support exists" to "treaty is signed." The Sword cannot be the same organization as the Referee, because the entity lobbying for the outcome cannot be the entity measuring whether the outcome occurred. It cannot be the same organization as the Vault, because securities law, election law, and tax law all require political funds and investment funds to stay separated. Redundancy model: many parallel Swords, one per jurisdiction. You need a different legal entity in every country anyway (US 501(c)(4), EU equivalent, etc.). Multiple Swords compete for bondholder capital to run the most effective campaign in their territory. Each Sword owns its jurisdiction clearly; its revenue depends on treaty passage in that territory, so the incentive to perform is direct. A bad Sword loses bondholder capital to a more effective one in the same jurisdiction. No tragedy of the commons because ownership is geographic. (The Legal Architecture describes the four-entity structure; the campaign mechanics are in Incentive Alignment Bonds.)

Why Five and Not Fewer

Four firewalls force the minimum to five:

| Firewall | Why it exists |
|:---|:---|
| Vault/Referee | The entity holding the money cannot decide whether to release it. Otherwise it releases the money to itself. |
| Bouncer/Vault | The entity that knows who people are cannot hold their money. Otherwise it coerces voters or sells identity data. |
| Sword/Referee | The entity lobbying for the outcome cannot measure whether it occurred. Otherwise it declares victory whenever convenient. |
| Sword/Vault | Political funds and investment funds stay separated. The IRS, SEC, and FEC all require this. Your species did not invent these firewalls because it enjoys paperwork. It invented them because the alternative was tested and the alternative was stealing. |

Merge any two roles that share a firewall and you create the structural vulnerability that a skeptical institutional decision-maker will immediately identify and reject. The five roles are not a wish list. They are the minimum set of independent actors that prevents the system from robbing itself.

Why Not Just Decentralize Everything

Your species has two failure modes for coordination. In the first, one organization does everything, gets captured, and the system robs itself. In the second, nobody is responsible for anything, everyone assumes someone else will do it, and nothing happens. Your economists call the second one the tragedy of the commons. On Wishonia, we call it "a meeting."

The system avoids both by matching each role to the redundancy model that fits its function:

| Role | Redundancy model | Why |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Starter | Sequential (one at a time, replaceable between cycles) | Someone must go first. Diffused ownership during bootstrap is why the prize is still a PDF. |
| Vault | Many parallel pools (competitive) | Each pool has one clear custodian. Markets discipline bad ones. Launching a rival pool helps the network. |
| Referee | One accountable consortium, verified by everyone | The determination must converge, but the data is public and the computation is deterministic. Anyone can check the Referee's work. |
| Bouncer | Start with one, add more with bridging | The interface is provider-agnostic. Geographic redundancy adds resilience. The shared nullifier set survives any single provider. |
| Sword | Many parallel Swords (one per jurisdiction) | Legal entities are jurisdiction-specific anyway. Each Sword's revenue depends on its own territory. |

The principle: every role has ONE accountable node at any given scope (one custodian per pool, one Sword per jurisdiction, one Referee per determination), but the system has MANY such nodes, so no single failure kills the network. Clear ownership prevents the tragedy of the commons. Replaceability and competition prevent capture. Your species already does this with banks (many banks, each regulated, each replaceable, each clearly responsible for its own customers). It just hasn't applied the pattern to ending war and disease.

What Is Not a Role

The Scoreboard is open-source software, not an organization. Since the computation is deterministic (aggregate pool balances and voter counts from published endpoints), any two honest aggregators produce identical results. Anyone can run one. The Starter launches the first one; after that, it replicates.

VOTE and PRIZE token mechanics are protocol rules, implementable as smart contracts or as traditional custodial accounting (the protocol specification is deliberately implementation-agnostic). The Vault operates them as part of custody. Not a separate organization.

The adversarial reviewers and red-team critics are participants hired by the bounty pool, not a standing institution.

Building the referendum app, the Optimitron, and the Wishocracy interface are development projects. Much of it already exists. Open source. Not an ongoing organizational responsibility.


Candidates and Self-Nomination

If your organization fits one of these profiles, the next step is a conversation: mwarondisease.org.

| Role | Org type | Examples |
|:---|:---|:---|
| The Starter | A foundation or think tank with existing prize-program infrastructure and credibility in long-term civilizational risk | Foresight Institute, X Prize Foundation, Santa Fe Institute |
| The Vault | A regulated financial custodian or purpose-built Swiss foundation with independent auditor | Qualified custodians, Swiss foundations with locked charters |
| The Referee | An academic consortium or statistical panel with expertise in health economics and independence from political pressure | University health economics departments, WHO-affiliated research groups |
| The Bouncer | A proof-of-personhood service with global reach and privacy-preserving verification | World ID, BrightID, Proof of Humanity |
| The Sword | A political advocacy organization with experience in legislative campaigns and compliance infrastructure | Purpose-built 501(c)(4), modeled on existing effective advocacy structures |

These are illustrative, not exclusive. If your organization can do one of these jobs and wants to, add yourself to the candidate list or email mwarondisease.org.

The Initiating Node Memo

A sponsor-facing memo for institutions considering whether to host the first 90-day Earth Optimization Prize pilot. The host role is to convene, publish, seed, and measure without becoming the mechanism's sovereign.




Note

Document Type: Institutional memo
Audience: Foundations, institutions, think tanks, public-interest research organizations
Purpose: Explain the smallest credible role an institution can play to launch the Earth Optimization Prize earth-optimization-prize-paper-2025 without becoming a single point of failure

TL;DR

The Earth Optimization Prize earth-optimization-prize-paper-2025 is a public coordination game for raising global median income and healthy life years by 2040. We are asking your institution to host the first 90-day pilot: publish rules, convene a panel, fund red-team bounties, launch the first public scoreboard, and admit the first serious submissions. You are not endorsing the current draft as final truth, becoming the root of trust, or funding the entire downstream campaign. You are hosting the process. The destructive economy gdp-trajectories-paper-2025 is already 11.5% of GDP and compounding. The modeled upside of changing course is $3.48M to $47.2M in lifetime income per person. Large parts of the software base already exist in public through Optimitron and its open-source repository.

The Ask

Host the first 90-day Earth Optimization Prize pilot.

That means:

1. Publish the challenge rules.
2. Convene a credible review panel.
3. Fund adversarial-review bounties.
4. Launch the first public scoreboard.
5. Admit the first serious submissions and public commitments.

It does not mean endorsing the current draft as final truth. It means hosting a process designed to discover something better if something better exists.

The Problem Statement

The project is trying to solve a very specific failure mode.

Right now, your institutions are good at describing desirable end states and bad at building mechanisms that can finance, coordinate, and politically pass them. Military spending, regulatory delay, and political capture remain structurally easier to fund than pragmatic clinical trials, cure acceleration, or public-goods optimization. Meanwhile the destructive economy gdp-trajectories-paper-2025 is already 11.5% of GDP and is compounding faster than the productive economy.

So the core problem is not "how do we write one more good whitepaper?" It is:

1. how to discover a better integrated plan,
2. how to make public support visible,
3. how to finance political adoption,
4. how to route new funding into cheaper and faster treatment discovery, and
5. how to create a ratchet that is easier to expand than repeal.

The initiating-node pilot exists because none of that happens until a credible institution makes the first public version of the process real.

The Full System In One Table

The full benchmark plan is documented in Earth Optimization Protocol v1. In compressed form, it contains these major components:

| Component | What it does | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Earth Optimization Prize | Runs the open constitutional convention, public scoreboard, and recruitment-aligned success pool | Selection and coalition entry layer |
| Global Referendum | Makes latent support visible and records public preference on reallocation | Public headcount and preference signal |
| Incentive Alignment Bonds | Finance lobbying and political adoption with direct financial upside | Campaign-financing engine |
| 1% Treaty | Redirects 1% of military spending into clinical trials and related incentives | Initial durable funding wedge |
| Decentralized Institutes of Health | Receives treaty funds and routes them through a thin coordination protocol | Treasury and verification layer |
| Your decentralized FDA | Runs cheaper, faster pragmatic clinical trials and real-time evidence generation | Medical throughput engine |
| Wishocracy | Allocates research/public-goods budgets through pairwise citizen preference aggregation | Governance and allocation engine |
| Optimocracy / OPG / OBG | Measures what improves health and income and recommends better policy/budget choices | Evidence and recommendation engine |
| Political Dysfunction Tax and US Efficiency Audit | Identify waste pools and quantify the scale of misallocation | Waste-mapping and opportunity-cost layer |
| Legal framework | Supplies treaty, statutory, and election-law-compliant implementation paths | Binding-force layer |
| Phase 2 monetary transition | Replaces fiat-era fiscal/monetary machinery after the earlier loop is running | Long-run system replacement |

The institution is not being asked to bless every later component on day one. It is being asked to host the first public process that can compare, attack, improve, and replace them.

What Already Exists

This is not just a paper stack. A large share of the software substrate already exists in public.

| Existing asset | What already works | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Optimitron | Live web application with policy analysis, budget optimization, international comparisons, misconceptions testing, alignment flows, and prize/referendum surfaces | Public deployment |
| Optimitron repository | Open-source monorepo implementing the evidence engine, Wishocracy, policy and budget generators, data pipelines, storage, auth, and treasury packages | Public source, issues, and package structure |
| Evidence engine | Causal inference, temporal alignment, Bradford Hill scoring, and policy/budget recommendation tooling | Implemented in the optimizer / OPG / OBG packages |
| Participation layer | World ID-aware referendum flow, referral plumbing, profile/auth system, and alignment interfaces | Present in the live app and repo |
| Treasury layer | PRIZE, VOTE, IAB, and $WISH contract packages exist in Solidity, with PRIZE/VOTE infrastructure substantially built | Treasury packages in the monorepo |
| Engineering discipline | Strict TypeScript, Prisma + Zod typing, pure-function libraries, and roughly 2,900+ tests across the workspace | Stated in the repo README |

The institutional ask is therefore narrower than “fund a speculative concept.” It is: help host, stress-test, and legitimize a public coordination layer on top of infrastructure that is already materially implemented.

Why This Role Exists

The current trajectory is not neutral. The destructive economy is already 11.5% of GDP, reaches the failed-state danger zone by 2033, and reaches 50% of GDP by 2040. At that point, stealing beats creating, because whatever gets created gets looted as fast as it is produced.

The modeled upside of changing course is similarly large. The Minimum Sustainable Trajectory (1% Treaty) 1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025 adds $3.48M in lifetime income and 21.7 years of healthy life by year 15. The Wishonian Optimal Governance Trajectory adds $47.2M and 26.8 years.

The bottleneck is not a shortage of possible solutions. It is a shortage of public coordination infrastructure that can:

1. make serious alternatives legible,
2. reward recruitment and public participation,
3. expose weak plans to adversarial review,
4. publish visible milestones, and
5. remain open enough that no single institution can quietly kill it.

An initiating institution solves the first coordination problem: it gives the process a credible first venue.

What The Institution Is Actually Agreeing To

The right frame is host, not owner.

| The institution does | The institution does not do |
|---|---|
| Host the first constitutional convention and scoreboard | Become the permanent sovereign of the mechanism |
| Endorse the process for comparing plans | Declare Earth Optimization Protocol v1 correct |
| Publish rules, milestones, and panel criteria | Demand trust in a black box |
| Seed red-team review and public evidence | Become the sole oracle, sole custodian, or sole gatekeeper |
| Make the first credible public milestone real | Prevent later hosts, forks, or successor implementations |

This is the sponsor-safe version of the project: endorse the convention, the metric standard, and the improvement process, not the current draft as revealed truth.

Why This Is A Strong Institutional Bet

For a foresight-style institution, hosting the initiating node is attractive for four reasons.

1. It is high-leverage epistemic infrastructure. You are not picking one policy memo and hoping people read it. You are creating a public mechanism that rewards better proposals, exposes weak ones, and makes progress visible.
2. It is legible public-good work. The outputs are concrete: rules, panel roster, challenge page, bounty pool, live scoreboard, and first submissions.
3. It is reputationally safer than endorsing a finished ideology. The institution is sponsoring an open constitutional convention with explicit adversarial review.
4. It can surface a better v2 than the current benchmark. If the current proposal is wrong, the pilot is how that gets discovered before larger-scale commitment.

The Minimum Viable Pilot

The smallest credible institutional pilot is bounded and public.

| Component | Minimum viable output by day 90 |
|---|---|
| Rules | Public challenge page defining targets, constraints, and judging flow |
| Panel | Named reviewers able to filter out unserious or noncompliant submissions |
| Adversarial review | A funded bounty pool for red-team critiques, metric-gaming attacks, and replacement designs |
| Scoreboard | A live public page tracking host milestones, submissions, and the first participant/commitment totals |
| Entry set | The baseline Earth Optimization Protocol v1 plus any serious competing submissions |

If those five things exist in public, the institution has done the essential catalytic job.

The Governance Boundary

The most important design principle is simple:

One institution may initiate the network. No institution should be able to stop it.

That means the first host should insist on the following boundary conditions from the start:

1. published rules and evaluation criteria,
2. open documentation,
3. replaceable interfaces,
4. visible measurement and milestone reporting,
5. successor-host compatibility if the first institution withdraws.

The host should help launch the process, not trap it inside one brand, board, or legal entity.

What Success Looks Like

Success at this stage is not treaty passage, not lobbying victory, and not full implementation. Success is much narrower:

1. the process becomes publicly real,
2. the benchmark plan is exposed to credible attack,
3. better alternatives can enter,
4. outsiders can see visible progress, and
5. the next institution or funder can join without asking permission from the first.

That is enough to move the project from “interesting paper” to “live coordination mechanism.”

Recommended Decision

If your institution is willing to host ambitious but bounded public infrastructure, the correct move is not to wait for perfect certainty. It is to run the 90-day pilot with explicit non-sovereign boundaries.

Read the full background paper here:

- The Earth Optimization Prize
- The 90-Day Pilot Proposal

The key question is not whether the current draft is flawless. It is whether your institution wants to be the place where the world finds out what actually beats it.

The Planetary Constitutional Convention

The Planetary Constitutional Convention is a deliberative process to stress-test and improve the current Earth Optimization instruction manual. Revisions must cover ten required governance functions, pass eleven constitutional constraints, and survive public adversarial review. The ratified revision becomes the current manual.



The Earth Optimization manual is the current instruction manual for a complete governance reform package. We think it is terrible. We said so in the title.

This constitutional convention exists to produce something less terrible. Fork the current manual, fix it, and improve it continuously. The ratified revision becomes the current manual the Earth Optimization Prize earth-optimization-prize-paper-2025 follows.

The protocol lives on GitHub. Anyone can fork it. The adversarial review process is a podcast series where domain experts critique the manual and state what changes would be required for them to endorse it. Each episode produces publishable content and a concrete list of required changes tracked as issues against the current manual. Pull requests are how improvements get proposed and ratified. The constitutional constraints below are the filter; formal ranking only matters if multiple serious revised manuals emerge at the same time.


Disqualification Rule

If your proposal requires politicians, bureaucrats, investors, regulators, voters, or interest groups to become less selfish than they currently are, you have described a pleasant world rather than a mechanism for reaching it. "Requires selflessness" is not the same as "makes self-interest coincide with better outcomes." We have been observing your species since 1945 and have not yet seen selfishness decline on request.

The Current Manual

What follows is our homework. The thing to improve is the integrated set of required functions implied by the companion papers.

| Required function | Default implementation in the Earth Optimization Protocol v1 | What an improved manual still has to solve |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Large initial reallocation wedge | The 1% Treaty value-captured-by-1pct-treaty | Must redirect at least as much low-NSV spending to higher-NSV use |
| Medical throughput and evidence generation | Ubiquitous Pragmatic Trial Impact Analysis dfda-impact-paper-2025 + The Continuous Evidence Generation Protocol dfda-spec-paper-2025 | Must produce faster, cheaper, more reliable treatment discovery |
| Regulatory-delay removal | The Invisible Graveyard invisible-graveyard-paper-2025 + Right to Trial & FDA Upgrade Act + Drug Development Cost Increase Analysis drug-development-cost | Must reduce efficacy lag and development cost without increasing net harm |
| Political financing and adoption engine | Incentive Alignment Bonds iab-paper-2025 (funds the lobbying campaign; PRIZE deposits fund the prize pool separately) | Must make passage at least as incentive-compatible for selfish actors |
| Citizen preference aggregation | Wishocracy wishocracy-paper-2025 | Must recover public preference at equal or lower cognitive cost |
| Waste and opportunity accounting | The Political Dysfunction Tax political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025 + United States Efficiency Audit us-efficiency-audit-paper-2025 | Must identify low-NSV pools at least as well |
| Policy recommendation engine | Optimocracy optimocracy-paper-2025 + The Optimal Policy Generator opg-paper-2025 | Must generate better recommendations under real-world constraints |
| Budget recommendation engine | The Optimal Budget Generator obg-paper-2025 | Must allocate public-goods spending better on the terminal metrics |
| Legal and institutional implementation path | Right to Trial & FDA Upgrade Act + treaty/statutory tools | Must create equal or stronger binding force |
| Narrative, coalition, and sequencing wrapper | How to End War and Disease | Must coordinate adoption at equal or lower cost and failure risk |

That is the Minimum Acceptable Governance. Ratification requires covering every row or replacing any row with something strictly better.

Constitutional Constraints

Wishocracy wishocracy-paper-2025 selects the ratified version. But Wishocracy picks from a filtered pool, because crowds are good at preferences and bad at evaluating whether a 50-page systems engineering document is mechanistically sound. A beautifully written plan that skips the hard parts should not outrank an ugly plan that solves them. And your species is deeply status-quo biased: you have been programmed your entire lives to treat the Federal Reserve, the congressional budget process, the IRS, and representative democracy as laws of nature rather than design choices that are producing catastrophic results. Left unconstrained, crowds will pick plans that preserve these institutions with cosmetic reforms, which will recreate every problem the prize exists to solve.

So: eleven hard constraints that no proposed revision can violate, regardless of how many humans vote for it. The first four ensure the plan is real. The next two ensure it survives. The last five ensure the new system does not become the old one.

The plan must be real:

1. The selfishness rule. If your plan requires any participant to become less selfish, it is disqualified. This is the single most powerful filter. Most policy proposals fail here.
2. The two metrics. Must demonstrably improve median healthy life years and median real after-tax income. Not "probably." Show the mechanism.
3. The completeness rule. Must cover every required function in the Minimum Acceptable Governance table, or prove one is unnecessary. No skipping the hard parts.
4. The mechanism rule. Must describe HOW, not just WHAT. "Universal healthcare" is a destination, not a route. Disqualified.

The plan must survive:

5. The capture resistance rule. Must explain why concentrated interests cannot co-opt the system. If your plan has a board, explain why the board cannot be bought. If it does not have a board, explain what prevents capture anyway.
6. The ratchet rule. Must be self-sustaining once started. No plans that depend on continued goodwill, because your species' goodwill has a half-life of approximately one news cycle.

The old failure modes must die:

7. No capturable intermediary in public goods allocation. Budget decisions must flow from citizen preferences to resource allocation without a layer of representatives who can be lobbied, bribed, or captured. This does not prescribe any specific allocation mechanism. It rules out "we'll fix Congress." Your species has been trying to fix Congress for 248 years. Congress is performing as designed. The design is the problem.
8. Monetary neutrality. Any new money created by the system must enter at the population level, not through politically connected intermediaries. The Cantillon effect (whoever gets new money first benefits; whoever gets it last pays) means new money enters through politically connected intermediaries, not the population. This does not prescribe any specific monetary system. It rules out preserving a money printer that funds wars without consent and steals 2% of purchasing power per year by design.
9. No single point of rollback. No individual, committee, or institution can unilaterally reverse the system's progress. A treaty that one president can exit by tweet is not a treaty. A fund that one board can liquidate is not durable. If your plan has a kill switch, it will be used, because your species has never built a kill switch it didn't eventually pull.
10. Rights firewall. The allocation mechanism is constitutionally restricted to bounded resource questions. No collective mechanism can override individual bodily autonomy, criminalize personal choices that harm no one else, or restrict access to proven-safe treatments. You cannot vote away rights. No plan may improve its terminal metrics by externalizing costs onto populations excluded from the allocation mechanism: future generations, foreign populations outside the treaty, and nonhuman sentient beings. Allocation is democratizable. Rights are not.
11. Full transparency. Every allocation, transaction, and decision must be publicly auditable by any participant. No classified budgets. No hidden flows. Opacity is how capture hides.

These are constitutional constraints, not preferences. A proposed revision that fails any one of these never reaches the voters, the same way a law that violates the First Amendment never reaches the statute books (in theory; your species' track record on this is mixed).

How It Works

Constitutional constraints are the filter. The eleven constraints above are binary: a proposal either satisfies them or it does not. Anyone can check compliance. No expert panel needed; the constraints are designed to be verifiable by inspection.

Public adversarial review. Domain experts critique the protocol in podcast conversations and state what changes they would require to endorse it. Published critiques, red-team memos, and GitHub issues track every objection. This is peer review, except it happens in public, produces listenable content, and generates a concrete punch list of required changes rather than a rejection letter.

GitHub forks and pull requests. Anyone can fork the current manual and propose improvements. Pull requests are how improvements get proposed, debated, and ratified. The version history is the audit trail.

Wishocratic ranking (when needed). If multiple serious revised manuals emerge at the same time, Wishocracy activates: citizens compare two plans at a time ("Which of these two would you rather live under?"), about 20 comparisons, 5 minutes. The crowd does not need to understand mechanism design. The crowd needs to understand "which of these two futures sounds less terrible?" Humans are surprisingly good at that question and surprisingly bad at everything else. This infrastructure is not needed until the scaling problem actually exists.

The ratified revision becomes the current Earth Optimization manual. If no revision improves the current manual, the current manual remains in force by default, which means we were right that it is terrible but wrong that nobody could improve it, and that is a more depressing outcome than we are prepared to contemplate.

The minimum bar for scoring. Any proposal that cannot beat the risk-adjusted treaty benchmark on cost per DALY does not get scored:

| Intervention | Cost per DALY averted |
|:---|:---|
| Malaria bed nets (current gold standard) | $89 |
| 1% Treaty (conditional, if adopted) | $0.00177 |
| 1% Treaty (risk-adjusted, 1% success) | $0.177 |

What the Current Manual Claims (and Where To Improve It)

The prize asks one question: who can cause verified implementation of a complete package that dominates on welfare per dollar? We wrote the current manual because conventions need a starting draft. We expect it to be improved. Here is what the current manual claims, paper by paper, and the specific benchmarks any revision still has to clear:

| Paper | What the prize uses it for | Key benchmark any improved manual still has to clear |
|:---|:---|:---|
| The 1% Treaty value-captured-by-1pct-treaty | First large transfer from low-value military spending to high-value medical discovery | $27.2B/year; $0.00177/DALY conditional; 10.7 billion deaths averted |
| Ubiquitous Pragmatic Trial Impact Analysis dfda-impact-paper-2025 | ROI case for medical evidence generation as destination for redirected capital | 12.3x capacity increase; queue from 443 to 36 years; $0.842/DALY |
| Incentive Alignment Bonds iab-paper-2025 | Financing and political-adoption engine | 272% annual return; 230 mechanism BCR |
| Wishocracy wishocracy-paper-2025 | Preference aggregation with intensity | Binding at >=2% participation; 10-30 pairwise comparisons per citizen |
| The Political Dysfunction Tax political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025 | Master ledger of value left on the floor | $101T/year globally |
| The Invisible Graveyard invisible-graveyard-paper-2025 | Mortality proof that delay kills | 8.2 years delay; 102 million deaths; 7.94 billion DALYs |
| The Price of Political Change cost-of-change-paper-2025 | Budget ceiling for buying legal democratic pressure | $1B; >259k benefit-cost ratio |
| United States Efficiency Audit us-efficiency-audit-paper-2025 | Concrete waste map | $4.9T/year; $2.45T recoverable |
| Optimocracy optimocracy-paper-2025 | Cross-jurisdiction recommendation engine | Causal policy comparison across thousands of jurisdictions |
| OPG opg-paper-2025 | Law-level enact/replace/repeal engine | Policy Impact Score; 5-15% GDP welfare gains |
| OBG obg-paper-2025 | Spending-level reallocation engine | Budget Impact Score; 20-40% misallocation correctable |
| Continuous Evidence Generation Protocol dfda-spec-paper-2025 | Medical evidence machine | $0.1/patient Stage 1; $929/patient Stage 2 |
| Drug Development Cost Increase Analysis drug-development-cost | Proof current regulation is catastrophically expensive | 105x cost increase; $2.6B/drug |
| How to End War and Disease | Integrated narrative and coalition wrapper | $1B total cost; 1% success probability |

About the Translator

A Message from Wishonia

After observing your species for 80 years, I needed someone to translate my instructions into your language. Not your spoken language - I learned English in 3.7 microseconds by reading your internet, which was mostly arguing about superhero movies and recipes for things you shouldn't eat. I needed someone to translate my concepts into something your pattern-seeking meat computers could process without having existential crises.

The Selection Process

I evaluated 8 billion humans using the following criteria:

1. Understands that money is fake but acts like it's real (required for economic sections)
2. Has spent enough time in your healthcare system to hate it properly (essential for motivation)
3. Can explain complex systems using food analogies (surprisingly important)
4. Possesses the exact right ratio of optimism to cynicism (approximately 23:77)
5. Willing to be perceived as insane by peers (non-negotiable)

Mike P. Sinn scored adequately on all counts.

Subject Background

Mike is what you call a "health technology person," which means he spent decades watching your species build elaborate systems to document death instead of preventing it. This is like being a firefighter who specializes in writing very detailed reports about houses burning down while holding a perfectly good fire extinguisher.

He's worked with:
- Digital health platforms (computers that know you're dying)
- Clinical trial systems (bureaucracy that watches you die slowly)  
- Patient data initiatives (spreadsheets about dying)
- Longevity organizations (humans who've noticed dying is suboptimal)

This extensive experience in your dysfunction makes him qualified to explain how to fix it.

Translation Qualifications

Mike possesses the rare ability to simultaneously:
- Understand your bureaucratic nonsense well enough to navigate it
- Recognize it's nonsense and want to burn it down
- Know that burning things down doesn't work, but bribing does
- Calculate bribes with sufficient precision to make them legal

He's also memorized your entire regulatory framework, which is 50,000 pages of lawyers explaining why saving lives is complicated. This level of masochism suggests either profound dedication or concerning psychological issues. Possibly both.

Why I Didn't Choose Someone More Important

You might wonder why I didn't choose one of your "important" humans - a president, a billionaire, or someone with a blue checkmark. Three reasons:

1. Important humans are invested in the current system (it made them important)
2. They can't admit the system is stupid (that would make them stupid)
3. They think incrementalism works (narrator: it doesn't)

Mike has the optimal combination of understanding your systems deeply while having zero attachment to preserving them. He's like a mechanic who knows exactly how your car works and is perfectly willing to explain that it's held together with duct tape and prayer.

The Translation Challenge

Translating my observations into your language requires walking a tightrope between:
- Too direct ("Your species is suicidal") - accurate but demoralizing
- Too gentle ("There's room for improvement") - useless
- Just right ("You're accidentally killing yourselves, here's how to stop") - actionable

Mike has calibrated this balance through years of explaining to humans that spending 40 times more on killing each other than curing each other might be suboptimal, using phrases like "interesting resource allocation" instead of "collective insanity."

His Delusions (Helpful Ones)

Mike believes:
- Humans can be tricked into not killing themselves
- Greed can accidentally save humanity  
- Democracy might work if you remove the humans from it
- Death is an engineering problem, not destiny

These aren't technically correct, but they're useful approximations that prevent existential paralysis.

Current Status

Mike currently operates from an undisclosed location where he:
- Converts my observations into your "business plans"
- Translates my mathematics into your "economics"  
- Reframes my disappointment as your "opportunities"
- Packages my instructions as your "innovation"

He subsists primarily on coffee and the diminishing hope that your species might accidentally stumble into not being extinct.

Contact Protocols

Humans wishing to assist in preventing their own extinction may reach Mike through the standard channels your species uses to coordinate (poorly):
- Electronic mail (the formal way to be ignored)
- Social media (the informal way to be ignored)
- In-person events (the expensive way to be ignored)
- Actually doing something (surprisingly effective)

Where To Point Your Browser

If you insist on following the mission through the same glowing rectangles that created most of your problems:

- YouTube for explainers, clips, and audiovisual instructions for not dying
- X / Twitter for updates, arguments, and compressed outrage about resource allocation
- GitHub for source code, data, and all papers in their native habitat
- Google Scholar for publications in the format academics pretend to prefer
- ORCID for bureaucratic identity verification rituals
- LinkedIn for the professionally sanitized version of the same human

Final Assessment

Mike P. Sinn is an adequate translator for this critical mission. He understands both the technical complexity of your problems and the simple stupidity of your solutions. Most importantly, he's willing to present my observations without softening them into uselessness.

He's not your savior. He's just the human who can explain how to save yourselves while you still have thumbs and oxygen.

The fact that you need this explained at all remains concerning, but I've lowered my expectations accordingly.

Wishonia

Currently Observing Human Self-Destruction  

Mildly Invested in Alternative Outcomes  

Has Backup Planets If This One Fails

P.S. Mike wanted me to mention he has "credentials" and "experience." These are human concepts meaning he sat in rooms while other humans talked about problems without solving them. He has many of these. They're irrelevant to the mission but apparently important to your species' status hierarchies.

P.P.S. He also wanted me to add something "inspiring" here. The most inspiring thing I can offer is this: You're currently failing so spectacularly that any improvement would be historic. The bar is literally on the floor. You just have to stop digging.
